errorRules.message: Thinking Machines answered HTTP 401. Check {apiKeyEnvVar}. Get a key at {setupUrl}

instructions: 1. Visit: https://tinker.thinkingmachines.ai/keys — the Quickstart (https://tinker-docs.thinkingmachines.ai/tinker/quickstart/) says "Or create an API key in the Tinker Console and set it as the TINKER_API_KEY environment variable."; an unauthenticated GET of that URL redirects to a page titled "Sign in" (sign-in was not attempted while building this entry)

2. Authentication as the vendor states it: the OpenAI-compatible page (https://tinker-docs.thinkingmachines.ai/tinker/compatible-apis/openai/) says "Authenticate with your Tinker API key, by passing the same key used for Tinker as the API key to the OpenAI client."; its code example reads the key from TINKER_API_KEY

3. Billing as the vendor states it: the Quickstart (https://tinker-docs.thinkingmachines.ai/tinker/quickstart/) says "Set up payment info in Billing, and see Models & Pricing for current training and sampling rates." (the Billing link goes to https://tinker.thinkingmachines.ai/billing/), and the Models & Pricing page (https://tinker-docs.thinkingmachines.ai/tinker/models/) says "All prices are per million tokens."
4. Set {apiKeyEnvVar} in your .env file (the vendor's examples read TINKER_API_KEY, which NeuroLink accepts as a fallback)
setup.description: Docs-verified only: the vendor's GET https://tinker.thinkingmachines.dev/services/tinker-prod/oai/api/v1/models needs a key (an unauthenticated GET on 2026-09-29 answered HTTP 401 with the JSON body {"detail":"X-Api-Key token is empty"}), so the twelve model ids come from the Training table on https://tinker-docs.thinkingmachines.ai/tinker/models/ (retrieved 2026-09-29) and the roster has not been checked; the entry is not yet live-verified. OpenAI-compatible endpoint at https://tinker.thinkingmachines.dev/services/tinker-prod/oai/api/v1: the OpenAI-compatible page (https://tinker-docs.thinkingmachines.ai/tinker/compatible-apis/openai/, titled "OpenAI API Compatible Inference (in beta)") says "The new interface exposes an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API.", gives that base URL, says "We support both /completions and /chat/completions endpoints." and says "Currently, OpenAI-compatible inference is meant for testing and internal use with low internal traffic, rather than large, high-throughput, user-facing deployments." The same page says "Use a Tinker sampler weight path as the model name." and shows a sampler weight path that begins with tinker://. moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6 is the catalog id that the OpenCode tutorial (https://tinker-docs.thinkingmachines.ai/tutorials/deployment/opencode/) shows as a models entry under the "Using a base model (no fine-tuning)" heading; the other eleven catalog ids are Tinker IDs from the Models & Pricing Training table. A tinker:// path passed as the model is an id outside the catalog. Unauthenticated GETs made 2026-09-29: /models answered HTTP 401 (content-type application/json) with the body {"detail":"X-Api-Key token is empty"}; /chat/completions answered HTTP 405 with header allow: POST and the body {"detail":"Method Not Allowed"}; the base URL itself answered HTTP 404 with the body {"detail":"Not Found"}. No POST request was sent. errorRules holds one rule, for the 401 status observed on /models. pricingPerMTok input is the Prefill figure, output is the Sample figure and cachedInput is the cached Prefill figure of each Training-table row; the page's Pricing Terms define Prefill as "Processing input/prompt tokens when sampling" and Sample as "Generating output tokens". models.defaultContextWindow (32768) is the figure in the OpenCode tutorial's Config fields table (https://tinker-docs.thinkingmachines.ai/tutorials/deployment/opencode/): "Max input tokens (32768 for most Tinker models)"; models.defaultMaxOutputTokens (8192) is the "output" figure in both example configs of that tutorial, whose Config fields table describes limit.output as "Max output tokens"; the catalog rows do not set maxOutputTokens, so the default applies to them. capabilities.text is true because the page documents /chat/completions; capabilities.streaming is true because the page describes streaming on /chat/completions ("In streaming mode, reasoning_content and content arrive on separate SSE events"); capabilities.thinking is true because the page documents the separate_reasoning flag and the reasoning_effort parameter on /chat/completions ("Not all models support this parameter."). capabilities.tools, toolsWithStreaming, structuredOutput and structuredOutputWithTools are false, meaning not declared by this entry: with tools false the provider's supportsTools() answers false and no tools array is sent, and no POST request exercising these was sent. capabilities.embeddings is false, not declared. billingPolicy no-free-tier is a schema placeholder (the schema has no unknown value), not a vendor statement. apiKeyFormat is null so NeuroLink's key-format check is not applied. Verification level: docs-verified, not yet live-verified.
